svg.title: Simplify: fewer triangles, same shape
svg.desc: Simplify costs every edge by the quadric error of collapsing it, collapses the cheapest first until about half the triangles are left, refuses unsafe collapses (borders, pinches, folds), and stores the result as one undo step without UVs, creases and seams.
svg.text: Simplify (retopology, first step)
Cut a dense mesh down to fewer triangles while the shape stays as close as possible.
1. Cost of every edge
Each point has a quadric: the sum of
the planes of its faces (by area).
An edge costs how far the merged
point drifts from those planes.
Flat areas cost almost nothing.
2. Collapse the cheapest
A heap picks the cheapest edge; the two
points become one at the best of: either
end or the middle. Neighbour costs are
recomputed. Stops at about half
of the triangles (SIMPLIFY_KEEP).
3. New mesh, one undo step
Unused points dropped, the rest
renumbered. UV map, creases and
seams are removed, and the message
says so. Press again for half of
that; Undo brings it back.
Safety rules (a collapse is refused if...)
- either end is on an open border or hard
edge and so is the other (both pinned)
- the edge is not shared by exactly two
triangles, or the neighbours would pinch
- a neighbouring face would turn over
Next: the rest of retopology
Retopo mode: draw quads over a dense
mesh, snapping to its surface.
Shrinkwrap: pull a rough mesh onto a
target. A target-count slider for
Simplify with a live preview.
